drhp.business: Jai Corp's operating business is its Plastic Processing Division, which makes tape woven products from polypropylene/polyethylene, including FIBCs, for domestic and export customers. Its steel division at Nanded, Maharashtra (cold rolled coils, galvanized coils and galvanized corrugated sheets) has been discontinued and its assets are being disposed of. Through subsidiaries it holds land as long-term investments, develops an industrial estate near Mumbai (Swar Land Developers Limited) and earns rental income from labour accommodations in the UAE (Oasis Holding FZC).

risks.body:

- The MD&A names raw-material availability among the normal industry risks the Company faces.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Exit a discontinued division: its operations have been discontinued and the Company is disposing of its assets. The same passage reports Nil GP/GC steel coil and sheet production.
- Plastics exports follow a policy of concentrating on high value products.
- Land acquired by subsidiaries is held as long-term investments and may be consolidated for development, subject to the legislation applicable at that time.
- Monetise the industrial estate near Mumbai: Swar Land Developers Limited has completed Phases I, II and III, which are being disposed of.

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
